claims.text: Ti40Zr40W10Mo10 is a dual-phase refractory high-entropy alloy investigated as an energetic structural material.
Ti40Zr40W10Mo10 has a BCC matrix containing Mo-W-rich BCC precipitates.
The untreated alloy contains a high density of Mo-W-rich precipitates.
Dislocation slip is the dominant deformation mechanism in untreated Ti40Zr40W10Mo10.
Refractory high-entropy alloys generally combine high strength with inferior plasticity or limited deformability.
Introducing a low atomic-percent concentration of interstitial nitrogen into the alloy will modify its stacking-fault energy.
Interstitial nitrogen alters the local electronic environment and defect interactions in a high-entropy-alloy matrix.
Interstitial nitrogen lowers the barrier for twin nucleation in Ti40Zr40W10Mo10 under dynamic loading.
Nitrogen doping will produce more uniformly distributed mechanical twinning during dynamic loading.
Mechanical twinning acting with dislocation slip can promote strain hardening and distributed plastic deformation, improving ductility without necessarily sacrificing strength.
Elevated strain rates above approximately 1000 s−1 promote twinning and can suppress shear localization in CrCoNi-based HEA/MEAs.
Nitrogen-doped Ti40Zr40W10Mo10 will have greater uniform ductility and less localized plastic deformation than the untreated alloy at about 3000 s−1.
Untreated Ti40Zr40W10Mo10 can sustain a compressive strength of approximately 2300 MPa at a strain rate of 3000 s−1.
The nitrogen-doped alloy will retain a compressive strength on the order of 2300 MPa.
Untreated Ti40Zr40W10Mo10 exhibits deflagration during dynamic deformation and therefore has potential for impact-induced energy release.
Nitrogen doping will preserve efficient impact-induced energy release.
The beneficial effect will hold from ambient to moderately elevated temperatures while the dual-phase microstructure is retained.
Only a narrow nitrogen-concentration range will be beneficial, while excess nitrogen may cause embrittlement or adverse microstructural changes.
